newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Bodies litter streets in anarchic Zairean border town.
newsitem.headline: Bodies litter streets in anarchic Zairean border town.

text.p: Bodies littered the streets and mobs chased suspected renegades and looters in the anarchic Zairean border town of Kasumbalesa on Saturday as rebels turned on allies who refused to lay down their arms.

Three bodies of armed young men lay in the dust in the centre of the small town on the Zambian border 95 km (55 miles) south of Lubumbashi, Zaire's second city and its copper capital that fell to the rebels earlier in the week.
At least one lay face down, his arms tied behind his back with a pink cloth. It was not clear if he had been shot or beaten to death.

Residents said at least seven more dead lay nearby, all local youths who had declared the town on Wednesday for Laurent Kabila's rebels, but refused to hand over their guns when Kabila's real troops arrived at dusk on Friday.
"There were about 50 of them holding out and they ran off into the bush, but some got trapped up by the border," said one man.
"There was lots of shooting last night and some bullets strayed across the border. The Zambians sent a note asking for an explanation of what was going on."
Local people were taking their revenge on Saturday, swarming to grab and stone suspected renegades.

They accuse them of looting and robbing round town during the two-day interregnum between the local collapse of President Mobutu Sese Seko's authority and the arrival of two trucks carrying Kabila's forces.
Locals said the dead men had been killed not by the mob but by rebel soldiers who had headed out of the town in pursuit of those who fled.
Some people said the youths were from JUFERI, the militant wing of a party that seeks autonomy for the mineral-rich southern Shaba province.

Its leader, Shaba governor Kyungu wa Kumwanza, is trying to cling to power by cooperating fully with the new authorities of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, who now control Shaba and half of Zaire.

Kabila's soldiers were nowhere to be seen in Kasumbalesa on Saturday, giving people a free rein to mete out summary justice. However, three trucks carrying scores of rebels were heading to the town on the one main road, from Lubumbashi.

Among those reportedly on the run was Colonel Kapenda, the Zairean army turncoat who had run up the white flag on Wednesday to signify support for Kabila but who had made off with some $10,000 from the customs post, locals said.
The border was closed. People said there were no officials left to speak of and the man who had the key to the barrier could not be found.
